one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent locked into a two-point (or two-level) distribution family with insufficient degrees of freedom to simultaneously satisfy both KL divergence targets within tolerance, then saved a noncompliant distribution and declared task completion despite errors ~3x larger than tolerance.
t_err_evidence: At step 4, the agent commits to a two-point distribution (one token at probability a, remaining 149999 tokens at probability b) with only two unknowns but three constraints (normalization + KL_forward=10 + KL_backward=10), an overdetermined and structurally insufficient model. This is the decisive wrong assumption: the agent never verifies whether a two-point model can satisfy both KL targets simultaneously before adopting it as the core strategy.
t_commit_evidence: At step 11, the agent saves /app/dist.npy for the first time despite the best error being ~5.94 (far beyond the 0.002 threshold), explicitly printing 'Distribution saved for reference'. This action locks in the failing outcome: even if subsequent steps refine, the final file written at steps 12-13 is also noncompliant, confirming the commit at step 11.
t_surface_evidence: At step 5, the script prints 'Solution did not meet tolerance requirements' with Forward KL=11.917 and Backward KL=9.998, giving total error ~1.919. This is the first clear observable signal that the approach fails.
trigger_explanation: At step 4, the agent acts on the unverified assumption that a two-point distribution (single high-probability token + uniform remainder) is an adequate model for simultaneously satisfying KL(P||U)=10 and KL(U||P)=10. This assumption is false: a one-parameter family cannot generally achieve two independent KL targets simultaneously. The agent adopted this premise without mathematical verification and built the entire subsequent strategy around it.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5 outputs Forward KL=11.917, Backward KL=9.998, Error=1.919, and prints 'Solution did not meet tolerance requirements'. Step 6 repeats the same failure with error=1.919. Step 7 produces an exception 'f(a) and f(b) must have different signs'. Step 8 shows a diagnostic exploration revealing the KL function behavior. Step 9 gives error=8.42. These are all forewarnings before t_commit=11.
